Tooltip_DazedTransformer: Carries the controller's power across town. Run a cable to the controller or to another transformer. While the system has power it lights everything around it, as far as the controller reaches, and it can wire up a building.
Tooltip_DazedPower_CellEmpty: Empty bay. Drag a car battery here.
Tooltip_DazedPower_ChooseBuildings: Click a building or a player-built structure to add it or take it away. Anything this part reaches can be chosen.
Tooltip_DazedPower_Coverage: Coverage on your current floor. Green: supplying power. Amber: no power. Lights and appliances in reach glow green when switched on, white when switched off. Press Esc to hide.
Tooltip_DazedPower_NeedRagWater: You need a rag and some water.
Tooltip_DazedPower_Painted: Painted with the Brush Tool: not a working controller.
Tooltip_DazedPower_TooHeavy: Too heavy for what you are carrying.
Tooltip_DazedPower_UnwireBuildings: Stops powering the buildings this part wired. Its own reach stays.
Tooltip_DazedPower_WireBuilding: Powers every floor of the building this stands in or next to, whenever the system has power. Power can reach a few tiles past its walls. Whatever runs in there draws on the batteries.
Tooltip_Recipe_DazedPowerSkyReading: Knowledge of reading the coming weather from the sky.
Tooltip_DazedPower_AmpNone: You are not carrying a generator amplifier.
Tooltip_DazedPower_AmpWhat: Fit it: +50%% output, twice the wear. Needs a screwdriver.
Tooltip_DazedPower_FuelNoWood: You are carrying no logs, planks, branches or charcoal. Other fuel is listed below by name.
Tooltip_DazedPower_FuelTooBig: Won't fit: the firebox has room for {1} fire-h, and this is {2}.
Tooltip_DazedPower_FuelWoodTooBig: None of your wood fits in what is left of the firebox.
Tooltip_DazedPower_GenNoFuel: No propane: fill its tank or hook up a propane tank.
Tooltip_DazedPower_GenNoTank: You are not carrying a propane tank.
Tooltip_DazedPower_GenWrecked: Its engine is seized. Repair it first.
Tooltip_DazedAmplifier: A hot-rodded winding and regulator that bolts onto one generator: +50%% power, but it wears twice as fast. Right-click a generator to fit it.
Tooltip_DazedGearKitLow: Wider gearing. Easier on the legs, less on the wire — pedal longer, lighter, before Fatigue catches up.
Tooltip_DazedGearKitRacing: Tighter gearing off a road bike. More watts for the same pedaling, at a harder cost in Fatigue.
Tooltip_DazedGearKitStock: The gearing it was built with. No trade either way.
Tooltip_DazedPedalMakeshift: A bicycle frame bolted to a scrap-built dynamo rig. Crude, and it shows in the wattage, but it turns legs into current.
Tooltip_DazedPedalSalvaged: A salvaged bike frame on a welded stand, geared to an alternator. Better than makeshift, short of a real workshop build.
Tooltip_DazedPropaneMakeshift: A small engine on a propane regulator, belted to an alternator. Pull-start only, thirsty at light loads, and loud enough to bring the street. Runs on its own small tank or a propane tank hooked up to its port. Never run it under a roof.
Tooltip_DazedPropaneSalvaged: A home standby unit, the kind that sat beside a house waiting for the power to go. Set it to AUTO and it starts itself when the batteries run low and stops when they are full. Its own tank plus one propane tank on its port.
Tooltip_DazedSteamMakeshift: An oil drum boiler over a firebox, belted to a scavenged engine. Burns wood flat out whatever the batteries need, drinks water, and you can hear it a street away. Never let it run dry. Fuel is counted in fire-hours, as a campfire burns it: a log is 6, a plank 2, charcoal twice its weight in wood.
Tooltip_DazedSteamSalvaged: A water-heater boiler and a proper engine with a governor: when the batteries are full it eases the fire down to what the house is using. Still thirsty, still loud. Fuel is counted in fire-hours, as a campfire burns it: a log is 6, a plank 2, charcoal twice its weight in wood.
Tooltip_DazedWeatherVane: An arrow on a pivot that points into the wind. Keep it outdoors and it builds a record of where the wind comes from and how hard it blows there, including which way a fixed windmill should face.
Tooltip_DazedWindMakeshift: Barrel-cut blades on a car alternator, up a pole. No tail fin: it faces the way you set it down, so aim it where the wind usually comes from. Storms will hurt it.
Tooltip_DazedWindSalvaged: A salvaged rotor on a pipe mast, with a tail fin that keeps it facing the wind. Works day and night, winter and summer. A bad storm can still damage it.
Tooltip_DazedWindsock: A striped cloth sock on a swivel pole. It streams downwind and stands straight out at about 28 km/h, so you can tell at a glance which way the wind blows and whether it is worth building a windmill. Put it somewhere open.
Tooltip_DazedPower_SteamEmpty: The boiler is empty. Firing it dry will ruin it.
Tooltip_DazedPower_SteamIndoors: It needs open sky to draw its fire and clear its smoke.
Tooltip_DazedPower_SteamNeedFuel: There is nothing in the firebox.
Tooltip_DazedPower_SteamNeedStarter: You need matches or a lighter.
Tooltip_DazedPower_SteamNoFuel: You are carrying nothing that burns.
Tooltip_DazedPower_SteamNoWater: You need water in a bottle, pot or bucket.
Tooltip_DazedPower_SteamWrecked: It is wrecked. Repair it first.
Tooltip_DazedPower_PetrolNoFuel: No petrol: pour some in from a petrol can, or link a gas tank.
Tooltip_DazedPower_PetrolNoCan: You are not carrying a petrol can with petrol in it.
Tooltip_DazedPetrolMakeshift: A small petrol engine belted to an alternator. Pull-start only, thirsty at light loads, and very loud.
Tooltip_DazedPetrolSalvaged: A home standby unit run on petrol. Set it to AUTO and it starts itself when the battery runs low. Loud, but it keeps running while the fuel lasts.
Tooltip_DazedArrayMakeshift: Cannibalised cells on a scrap frame. Weak, and the weather eats it, but it is a panel and it is free.
Tooltip_DazedArraySalvaged: A proper tilted array. Point it south, keep it clear of roofs, sweep the snow off in winter.
Tooltip_DazedArrayWorkshop: Monocrystalline cells on an aluminium frame. Twice the array of the standard frame, and it barely notices the heat.
Tooltip_DazedBankMakeshift: Three car batteries strapped to a pallet. Small, leaky, and it hates being run flat.
Tooltip_DazedBankSalvaged: An open steel rack for six car batteries. Running it flat costs capacity for good.
Tooltip_DazedBankWorkshop: Eight sealed deep-cycle cells in a vented cabinet. Holds its charge in the cold and forgives a deep discharge.
Tooltip_DazedWallBankMakeshift: Two batteries on a plank shelf. Takes no floor space and not much else either.
Tooltip_DazedWallBankSalvaged: A three-cell box that bolts to a wall. Half the storage of the rack, none of the footprint.
Tooltip_DazedWallBankWorkshop: Four sealed cells in a wall cabinet. The tidy way to fill a battery room.
Tooltip_DazedControllerMakeshift: Ties the arrays and the banks together and powers everything nearby. Silent, unlike a generator.
Tooltip_DazedControllerWorkshop: Tracks each array's maximum power point. Ten per cent more out of the same panels, and a better readout.
Tooltip_DazedPedalWorkshop: A proper dynamo and flywheel on a welded frame. Built, not scavenged — the most watts a rider can put out of one of these.
Tooltip_DazedWindWorkshop: A proper three-blade turbine on a lattice tower. Tracks the wind, starts in a light breeze, and turns itself edge-on to ride out a storm unharmed.
Tooltip_DazedSteamWorkshop: A workshop plant: an efficient boiler, a muffled engine, and a condenser that turns most of its exhaust back into water. The most power from every log. Fuel is counted in fire-hours, as a campfire burns it: a log is 6, a plank 2, charcoal twice its weight in wood.
Tooltip_DazedPropaneWorkshop: A properly muffled standby generator with a bigger reservoir and two ports for propane tanks. The most power per tank, and the quietest of the three. AUTO starts and stops it around the batteries.
Tooltip_DazedPetrolWorkshop: A muffled workshop-grade petrol generator with a big tank. The most power per litre and the quietest of the petrol engines, though still loud.
Tooltip_DazedGardenLampMakeshift: A knee-high light with its own little panel and battery. It charges in the sun and lights the path from dusk to dawn. Needs no wiring. A jar-lid panel and a small cell: about 12 hours of light, so it goes out before dawn in winter.
Tooltip_DazedStreetLampMakeshift: A street light on a pole, with its own panel and battery pack. It charges all day and lights the road from dusk to dawn. Needs no wiring. About 12 hours of light on a full cell.
Tooltip_DazedGardenLampWorkshop: A solar garden lamp with a proper panel and cell: brighter, a wider pool of light, and 20 hours on a full charge, so it lasts the longest winter night. Never wired; charges where it stands.
Tooltip_DazedStreetLampWorkshop: A solar street lamp with a large panel and cell: the widest pool of light and 20 hours on a full charge, the whole night year-round. Snow on the panel still stops the charging. Never wired.
Tooltip_DazedTrackerMakeshift: A Makeshift solar array on a frame that turns to follow the sun in coarse steps: about 8%% more energy than the same array standing still. Wires to a controller like any array.
Tooltip_DazedTrackerSalvaged: A Salvaged solar array on a frame that follows the sun through the day: about 12%% more energy than the same array standing still. Wires to a controller like any array.
Tooltip_DazedTrackerWorkshop: A Workshop solar array on a smooth tracking frame: about 15%% more energy than standing still, and it tips itself to shed snow. Wires to a controller like any array.
Tooltip_DazedArrayXLMakeshift: Four Makeshift solar arrays on one welded frame. Covers 2x2 squares; one cable for the lot. Comes apart into parts to carry.
Tooltip_DazedArrayXLSalvaged: Four Salvaged solar arrays on one welded frame. Covers 2x2 squares; one cable for the lot. Comes apart into parts to carry.
Tooltip_DazedArrayXLWorkshop: Four Workshop solar arrays on one welded frame. Covers 2x2 squares; one cable for the lot. Comes apart into parts to carry.
Tooltip_DazedPowerManual: Teaches the Makeshift and Salvaged builds of every Dazed Power part: arrays, trackers, large arrays, battery banks, the Makeshift charge controller, the transformer, pedal, wind, steam and gas generators, and the low and stock gear kits.
Tooltip_DazedPowerManualAdv: Teaches the Workshop builds: arrays, trackers, large arrays, battery cabinets, the Workshop charge controller, the Workshop lamps, pedal, wind, steam and gas generators, and the racing gear kit.
Tooltip_DazedAlmanac: The county almanac. Read it to learn to read the sky: a reading gives you the next 29 days of weather as of the moment you took it.
Tooltip_DazedPower_WireCost: Uses {1} Electric Wire (you have {2}). Cutting it later gives half back.
Tooltip_DazedPowerGauge: Hang it on a wall and run a cable to any part of a system. It shows the battery charge, the watts coming in and going out, and the sources running, anywhere in the base. Takes no controller slot.
Tooltip_DazedPower_Priority: As the batteries run down, Low machines on this system are cut first, then Normal. Essential ones run until the low-voltage disconnect. Building lights and appliances are not affected.
Tooltip_DazedPower_ChargeUnwired: Wire this bench to a controller first.
Tooltip_DazedGroundingRod: A copper rod driven into the ground. Stand it within a few tiles of a controller and lightning goes to earth instead of through your system.
Tooltip_DazedChargerBench: Wire it to a controller. Charges loose car and small batteries from the system's racks, above the discharge floor, with some loss.
Tooltip_DazedWaterWheel: Set it at the edge of a stream or river and wire it to a controller. Steady power in any weather; ice slows it.
Tooltip_DazedPower_AdminRepair: Admin: set every part in this system to full condition, and each battery to the best its wear allows.
Tooltip_DazedPower_AdminReset: Admin: clear the breaker trip and the low-voltage disconnect, switch the system on, stop any equalisation and relink its wiring.
Tooltip_DazedPower_AdminFill: Admin: fill every battery rack in this system to its capacity.
Tooltip_DazedPower_AdminReach: Stand next to the controller to use this.
Tooltip_DazedElectricFence: Wire it to a controller. While the system is on and above its discharge floor, a zombie that comes up against it is knocked down and stunned, for a few watt-hours a zap. People are not hurt.
Tooltip_DazedRoomCooler: Hang it on a wall inside a room and wire it to a controller. While powered, food in every container in that room keeps like it does in a fridge. Draws 100 W plus 10 W for each container. With Dazed Climate it also chills the room's air.
Tooltip_DazedSpaceHeater: Stand it on the floor and wire it to a controller, then switch it on. Draws 1500 W while it runs. With Dazed Climate it warms the room it stands in.
